title: Learning to Decode Concatenated Quantum Codes with Hierarchical Message Passing
authors: Jiahui Wu, Chao Zhang, Zipeng Wu, Shilin Huang
abstract: We introduce a neural message-passing framework for decoding general concatenated stabilizer codes. Soft beliefs propagate bidirectionally across concatenation levels, and lightweight neural networks learn only to aggregate incoming messages. For the concatenated $[[15,7,3]]$ quantum Hamming code, the resulting decoder achieves substantially higher thresholds than the state-of-the-art bidirectional hard-decision decoder under both bit-flip and depolarizing noise. In particular, the depolarizing pseudo-threshold nearly doubles, from $6.5\%$ to $12.3\%$. For many-hypercube codes, a decoder fine-tuned on circuit-level errors in Knill's teleportation-based error correction can achieve lower logical-CNOT failure rates than their dedicated decoder, using a fixed number of message-passing iterations instead of extensive combinatorial search. Our framework provides a generic decoding tool for exploring the design space of concatenated codes, including non-CSS constructions, toward low-overhead fault tolerance.
summary: This work presents a novel neural message-passing decoder for decoding complex concatenated quantum error-correcting codes. By propagating soft beliefs across code levels, the decoder achieves substantial improvements in error thresholds compared to existing state-of-the-art methods. This framework offers a general tool for advancing fault-tolerant quantum computation design.
main_problem: The paper addresses the challenge of efficiently and accurately decoding general concatenated quantum error-correcting codes.
main_result: The proposed neural message-passing decoder significantly outperforms state-of-the-art hard-decision decoders, notably nearly doubling the depolarizing pseudo-threshold for the [[15, 7, 3]] Hamming code.
method: It introduces a neural message-passing framework where soft beliefs propagate bidirectionally across code concatenation levels, using lightweight networks only for message aggregation.
model_or_system: The model focuses on concatenated quantum stabilizer codes, tested on specific examples like the [[15, 7, 3]] Hamming code and many-hypercube codes. The framework is designed to be generic for exploring various code constructions.
key_observables: Pseudo-threshold ($p^*$) under bit-flip and depolarizing noise, and logical-CNOT failure rates.
important_parameters: The number of message-passing iterations (fixed for bounded latency), and the specific noise models (bit-flip, depolarizing).
main_assumptions: The core message-passing rules are kept fixed, departing from fully end-to-end neural decoders, and the initial state can be learned to capture circuit-level error distributions.
figures_summary: Figures compare block failure rates for the Hamming code and many-hypercube code under different noise types, demonstrating the decoder's superior performance compared to baseline decoders.
paper_structure: The paper details the neural message-passing architecture, presents results comparing its performance against hard-decision decoders on various code families, and discusses fine-tuning on circuit-level error data.
why_interesting: The use of neural networks to model complex, structured error correction processes provides a powerful, trainable tool for analyzing fault tolerance limits in quantum computation.

(a) Under bit-flip noise, the neural MP decoder raises the pseudo-threshold from p∗≈4.4% to 6.8%. (b) Under depolarizing noise, it nearly doubles the pseudo-threshold, from p∗≈6.5% to 12.3%.

Fig. 1 compares the neural MP decoder with the bidi- rectional hard-decision decoder [16] on the concatenated [[15, 7, 3]] quantum Hamming code [38, 39], which at level L encodes k = 7L logical qubits into n = 15L physical qubits. Each block carries 7 canonical logical triples plus 35 auxiliary weight-3 logical-observable triples, giving k′ = 42; k′′ = 14 of these are used to generate logical- observable triples at the next level.
